title: The Dome of the Rock
hookLine: a golden dome in Jerusalem over the rock linked with the night journey

lines: A BARE ROCK IN THE MIDDLE.
cards: Inside, the light drops. You come in from the bright stone plaza, and your eyes adjust. Columns of marble.
Gold mosaic catching what light there is. And in the middle, behind a railing, not a floor at all but a great bare outcrop of rock, rough and uneven, the hill itself coming up through the building.
Everything else was built around it. Above it, the dome. This is Jerusalem, on the high plaza Muslims call al-Haram al-Sharif, the Noble Sanctuary.
Today: the Dome of the Rock.

teach.h: BY NIGHT TO THE FARTHEST MOSQUE.
teach.b: Start with the journey. The Qur'an opens one surah with it: "Glorified be He Who carried His servant by night from the Inviolable Place of Worship to the Far Distant Place of Worship."
The Inviolable Place is the Kaaba in Mecca. The Far Distant Place, al-Masjid al-Aqsa, is understood in Islamic tradition as Jerusalem.

The hadith collections tell how, from there, the Prophet ﷺ was taken up through the heavens, and tradition links that ascent with this rock. The rock is holy in Jewish tradition too, on the hill where the Temple stood.
Now the building. Tradition says the Umayyad caliph Abd al-Malik had it raised over the rock.
Its plan is an octagon, with rings of columns, so pilgrims can walk around the rock beneath the dome. One distinction: the Dome of the Rock is not the mosque. It's a shrine.
The mosque for congregational prayer, al-Aqsa Mosque, stands at the southern end of the same plaza.

teach.h: VERSES IN GOLD, TILES IN BLUE.
teach.b: Look up inside and a long band of Arabic runs around the walls in gold mosaic: verses of the Qur'an, including verses about Jesus son of Mary, whom the Qur'an honors as a messenger.
Outside, the walls blaze with blue and white tiles, added in a later age, so the building has been dressed by more than one generation.
A city holy to many, a journey by night, and over the spot, a dome over the rock.

how: Muslims visiting Jerusalem pray at al-Aqsa Mosque and visit the Dome of the Rock on the same plaza, and the night journey is remembered on the night Muslims call al-Isra wal-Mi'raj.

o: the mosque at the south end of the plaza
the golden dome raised above the shrine
the rock: the bare stone at the shrine's center

games.q: the Dome of the Rock — tap the pairs.
p: Umayyad caliph, tradition says its builder

s: the Dome of the Rock is al-Aqsa Mosque
it is a shrine; al-Aqsa Mosque stands at the southern end of the same plaza.
a bare rock lies under the dome, with the building around it
the outcrop rises inside, behind a railing.
the inscriptions inside include Qur'anic verses about Jesus son of Mary
the gold mosaic band carries them.

games.q: you're designing a building over a rough, sacred rock. pilgrims will want to walk around it. what shape do you choose?
o: a long hall with the rock at one end.
an octagon with rings of columns around the rock.
flatten the rock and build a floor over it.
games.why: the builders made an octagon with rings of columns, so people can walk around the rock beneath the dome.

practice: If you can, look at a close photo of the outer tiles and follow one line of the pattern until it turns and meets itself, noticing the writing woven into the design.

Then close your eyes and picture the rock inside, untouched, with the whole building shaped around it. If you pray, you can recite the opening of Surah al-Isra: glorified be He who carried His servant by night.

wordCard.voice: Sakhrah, the rock itself: the bare stone at the center of the shrine, linked in tradition with the Prophet's night journey and holy in Jewish tradition too. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: the Dome of the Rock; sakhrah means rock.

carryVoice: Your line: a dome over the rock. Built around it, not over it. That's day nine hundred four.
